correctness.rationale: The two-world IS4 construction satisfies all frame and persistence conditions, and direct forcing proves failure of the target formula. For a one-world IS4 frame, modal reflexivity leaves exactly two valuations of the sole atom; if the atom is true then the first inner implication fails, and if it is false then the double-negation conjunct fails. Hence the boxed conjunction is false and the target formula true in both cases. The one-world IK4 frame with empty modal relation is transitive and confluent vacuously and makes the outer box true, so it falsifies the target. These arguments establish exact minima 2 and 1 without relying on finite experimentation.

value.rationale: The source itself uses the formula to motivate the need for loop control in a long-standing IS4 decidability problem. Determining its exact semantic model size shows that proof-search divergence can coexist with a smallest two-world countermodel, and the sharp IK4 comparison isolates reflexivity as the precise cause of the size increase. This is a motivated boundary fact, not an arbitrary enumeration.
